method.approach: Region-wave migration (ADR-015); rules executed against the Claims Hub PostgreSQL databases after cut-over
method.rehearsalData: Masked data for rehearsals (ADR-025); production data only in the cut-over run
method.tooling: Data migration reconciliation workspace (IBM Programme Skerry team)

ownership.businessSignOff: Aisha Siddiqui, Head of Claims Hub Product

summary.openDefectsNote: Open items are tracked in the CHUB project under the Wave 1 hypercare epic.

checks.rule: Column legacy_claim_id holds a value allowed by the target domain
checks.query: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM claim_core.claim t LEFT JOIN allowed a ON a.code = t.legacy_claim_id WHERE a.code IS NULL
checks.queryNote: allowed = target domain list for the column
checks.comment: The check compares the migrated value with the CLARA source after normalisation of currency and decimal places.

checks.rule: Mandatory column policy_no is populated for every migrated row
checks.query: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM claim_core.claim t WHERE t.policy_no IS NULL
checks.comment: In practice, results are reproducible from the reconciliation workspace using the stored query.

checks.rule: Primary key claim_id is unique in the target table
checks.query: SELECT claim_id, COUNT(*) FROM claim_core.claim GROUP BY claim_id HAVING COUNT(*) > 1
checks.comment: Operationally, the check compares the migrated value with the CLARA source after normalisation of currency and decimal places.

checks.rule: Column status carries the source time stamp converted to UTC
checks.query: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM claim_core.claim t WHERE t.status IS NOT NULL AND t.status > now()

checks.comment: Note that the check was first run in the rehearsals and kept unchanged for the production cut-over.
